slides.title: Modern OpenGL Pipeline
slides.prompt: OpenGL uses programmable Vertex and Fragment Shaders written in GLSL to process 3D vertex buffers into rendered pixels.
slides.codeSnippet:
from OpenGL.GL import *

# Buffer Allocation
vbo = glGenBuffers(1)
glBindBuffer(GL_ARRAY_BUFFER, vbo)
glBufferData(GL_ARRAY_BUFFER, vertices.nbytes, vertices, GL_STATIC_DRAW)

slides.title: Vertex vs Fragment Shader
slides.prompt: What is the specific responsibility of a GLSL Fragment Shader in the OpenGL graphics pipeline?
options: Computing final pixel color, lighting, and texture values for rasterized surfaces
Transforming 3D world space coordinates into 2D screen clip space coordinates
Compiling Python bytecode instructions into executable GPU binaries
Managing user keyboard and mouse input events
slides.correctAnswer: Computing final pixel color, lighting, and texture values for rasterized surfaces

slides.title: Vertex Array Objects (VAO)
slides.prompt: Why are Vertex Array Objects (VAOs) used in modern OpenGL execution loop architectures?
options: To store vertex attribute state configurations and pointer bindings into a single reusable state object
To automatically generate 3D mesh geometry models
To convert Python arrays into JPEG image files
slides.correctAnswer: To store vertex attribute state configurations and pointer bindings into a single reusable state object
